title: KDP Rejecting Your EPUB? How to Find & Fix Errors
excerpt: KDP EPUB errors range from minor warnings to hard rejections. This guide shows you how to identify every error type, what each one means, and the fastest way to fix them.

meta_description: KDP rejecting your EPUB? This guide covers every common EPUB error type — hard blocks, warnings, and content flags — with step-by-step fixes for each.
html:
KDP EPUB errors can stop your upload entirely or quietly degrade your book's quality. The problem is that KDP's error messages are often vague — "content error" or "structure issue" doesn't tell you which file, which line, or what actually went wrong.

This guide breaks down every major category of KDP EPUB error, what each one actually means, and how to fix it before your next upload.

The Difference Between Hard Errors and Warnings

KDP separates feedback into two categories, and the difference matters.

Hard errors block publication. Your book will not go live until you fix them and re-upload. These include missing TOC, invalid mimetype, corrupt file structure, and certain metadata problems.

Warnings don't block publication, but they degrade the reading experience. Deprecated HTML tags, unsupported CSS, and image sizing warnings fall here. KDP will publish the book, but readers may see formatting problems on older Kindle devices.

Fix hard errors first. Then address warnings systematically, starting with the ones most likely to affect visible formatting.

Hard Error: Invalid EPUB Package Structure

This error means KDP can't read the basic structure of your EPUB file. Common causes:

  • The mimetype file is missing, compressed, or not the first file in the ZIP archive
  • The META-INF/container.xml file is missing or points to a non-existent OPF file
  • The EPUB was zipped incorrectly — the top-level folder was included in the ZIP instead of the contents

To fix: unzip your EPUB, verify the structure, and repackage correctly. The mimetype file must be added to the ZIP first with the store (no compression) method. Many third-party ZIP tools compress it by default, which breaks the EPUB.

Hard Error: Missing or Invalid TOC

Your EPUB needs either an NCX file (EPUB 2.0) or a nav document (EPUB 3.0) with valid chapter links. If both are missing or the links are broken, KDP blocks the upload.

Run your file through the EPUB Validator to see exactly which TOC element is missing or broken. The TOC Generator can rebuild a valid table of contents from your manuscript headings if yours is missing entirely.

Hard Error: Malformed OPF Manifest

The OPF file lists every component of your EPUB. If a file listed in the manifest doesn't exist, or if a file that exists isn't in the manifest, KDP flags it as a structural error.

Open your OPF file in a text editor and compare the manifest item list against the actual files in your EPUB. Remove manifest entries for files that don't exist. Add entries for files that exist but aren't listed. Make sure every file path uses the correct relative path and file extension.

Hard Error: Invalid XML in Chapter Files

EPUB chapter files must be valid XHTML. If a chapter file has unclosed tags, mismatched tags, or characters that aren't properly escaped, KDP may reject the file.

Common XML problems:

  • Using & instead of & in text content
  • Unclosed <img> tags (should be <img .../>)
  • Smart quotes or em dashes that aren't UTF-8 encoded properly
  • HTML comments that contain double dashes: <!-- -- -->

Run your EPUB through the EPUB Validator to get a specific list of XML errors by file and line number. Manual fixes are straightforward once you know exactly what's wrong.

Warning: Unsupported CSS Properties

Kindle devices don't support all CSS properties. Properties like text-shadow, border-radius, certain flexbox properties, and position: fixed are ignored or cause rendering issues on older Kindle hardware.

KDP will flag these as warnings. The book publishes, but the unsupported CSS is stripped, which may change your layout. Review KDP's Kindle publishing guidelines for the current list of supported CSS, and remove or replace unsupported properties.

Warning: Deprecated HTML Tags

Tags like <font>, <center>, <b> (when used for styling rather than semantic emphasis), and <i> (same) generate warnings. Replace them with CSS equivalents. Use <strong> and <em> for semantic emphasis, and apply text alignment and font styling through your CSS file.

Warning: Image DPI or Size Issues

KDP recommends images at 96 DPI for interior images and at least 1600px on the longest side for covers. High-resolution print images (300 DPI) make your EPUB file very large without improving screen quality. Oversized images may also cause rendering slowdowns on older Kindle devices.

Before uploading, resize interior images to 96 DPI and compress them. Your cover should be at minimum 1600x2560px but doesn't need to be larger than 2500x4000px for most devices.

How to Audit Your EPUB Before Every Upload

Run every EPUB through the EPUB Validator before uploading anywhere. The validator checks structure, OPF, TOC, HTML validity, image references, and CSS — giving you a prioritized list of what to fix.

If you're starting from a Word document, running it through the Word Cleanup Checker first catches formatting problems at the source — before they become EPUB errors during conversion.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does KDP take to process an EPUB after upload?

Structural errors are usually flagged within minutes. Content review (for compliance) takes 24–72 hours. If you get an error within the first few minutes of upload, it's a structural problem you need to fix before the file even enters content review.

Can I fix EPUB errors without specialized software?

Yes. Most EPUB errors can be fixed in a text editor. EPUB files are just ZIP archives containing HTML, CSS, and XML. Unzip the file, fix the specific error in the relevant file, repackage correctly, and you're done. The challenge is knowing which file to edit and what to change — which is why a validator report is so useful.

Will fixing errors on an already-published book affect my sales or ranking?

No. Uploading a corrected version doesn't affect your book's sales history, reviews, or ranking. Readers who already bought it get the updated file automatically via Whispersync. The update usually propagates within 24–48 hours.

Does KDP have a limit on how many times I can re-upload?

No fixed limit, but frequent re-uploads on the same ASIN that result in rejections can slow down your review queue. Fix all known errors before each re-upload rather than trial-and-erroring through the system.

Is there a difference between EPUB errors and KDP content policy violations?

Yes. EPUB errors are technical problems with your file structure. Content policy violations are about what's in the book — pricing, copyright claims, prohibited content. Technical EPUB errors are flagged immediately on upload. Content policy reviews happen after the file is accepted structurally.
